limits_data.description: Single canonical table containing market risk limits, exposures, governance metadata and audit fields. Use this single table for daily monitoring, breach tracking and reporting.
limits_data.business_context: Source of truth for front-office and risk-monitoring limits. Contains limit definitions, current exposures, utilization, and lightweight audit/approval fields for breaches and temporary overrides.

key_columns.critical_note: ⚠️ CRITICAL: Many limit_groups start with letters (A., B., C., etc.). When users mention 'PV01', 'Gamma', 'Liquidity', etc., match against limit_group patterns like 'C. PV01 Curve Risk Limits' or use pattern matching. Example: 'PV01 limits' → WHERE limit_group LIKE '%PV01%' OR limit_group = 'C. PV01 Curve Risk Limits' (NOT limit_type - limit_type is 'PV01 Delta')

date.definition: Snapshot date (YYYY-MM-DD). Default to MAX(date) for latest data.
date.usage: WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) for latest, or date >= MAX(date) - INTERVAL 'N days' for trends

letter_nm.definition: Trading desk name (129 total desk names). Examples: 'Canadian Options', 'Oil Products NGL Trading', 'Canadian Government Bond Trading'
letter_nm.usage: Primary filter for desk queries. Use exact match for precision: WHERE letter_nm = 'Canadian Options'. For regional queries, can use ILIKE '%Canadian%' to match multiple Canadian desks. See business_glossary for regional patterns.

limit_id.definition: Unique identifier for the limit row
limit_id.usage: Use to reference specific limits. Not typically used in user queries unless referencing a known limit ID.

limit_class.definition: Governance level. Valid values: ex-ZNDRY, ex-PRIM, Inner RAL, Notice, Outer RAL, Primary (enforced), Reporting, Secondary
limit_class.usage: Default to WHERE limit_class = 'Primary' unless user specifies otherwise.

limit_group.definition: CRITICAL: Risk metric category. Many categories start with letters (A., B., C., etc.) like 'A. VaR & Stress Limits', 'C. PV01 Curve Risk Limits'. Total of 78 limit group categories. When user says 'PV01 limits', use pattern matching like WHERE limit_group LIKE '%PV01%'
limit_group.usage: WHERE limit_group LIKE '%PV01%' OR limit_group = 'C. PV01 Curve Risk Limits' (NOT limit_type). This is the top-level category users refer to.

limit_type.definition: Detailed sub-category (e.g., 'PV01 Delta', 'Gamma Vega'). May be very specific long strings like 'CR01 / Bond / ExclNon-Corporates / ExclCcn Banks / A+ / IG Corp' or 'Total Stress (w/ MSS) - MTM USD'. Total of 122 limit type values. Refines limit_group.
limit_type.usage: Use with limit_group for precise filtering. limit_type contains 'PV01 Delta', not just 'PV01'.

limit_desc.usage: Use text search (ILIKE) for flexible matching. Parse for product-level specifics when needed.

meas_unit.definition: Currency/unit with 27 variants: USD, CAD, EUR, JPY, AUD, BBL, BPS, BU, CHF, GBP, MT, MWH, MXN, NZD, OZ, Event, DAYS, etc. See data_samples for full list.
meas_unit.usage: Filter by currency: WHERE meas_unit = 'USD'. Cannot aggregate different units without conversion.

aggr_func_cd.definition: Aggregation method with 32 variants: GRID, GROSS, NET, GROSS BY SECURITY, SINGLE NAME, SINGLE INDUSTRY, NET LONG BY SEC, BY TRADE, etc. See data_samples for full list. Note: 'Pending Upload' is a data quality issue, not a valid value.
aggr_func_cd.usage: Determines if positions net or sum. Filter: WHERE aggr_func_cd LIKE '%NET%' or '%GROSS%'

rating_floor.usage: Apply rating filters for credit-limited buckets

unofficial_flag.usage: Filter WHERE unofficial_flag = 0 for enforced limits only

exposure_amt.usage: Compare to effective_limit. Used in utilization = exposure_amt / effective_limit

Original_limit.definition: Original approved limit value (baseline before adjustments)
Original_limit.usage: Used for audit. Compare to effective_limit to track changes

effective_limit.usage: Always use this (not Original_limit) for breach detection: utilization = exposure_amt / effective_limit

utilization.usage: Primary risk metric. Default sort: ORDER BY utilization DESC. Filter: WHERE utilization >= 0.9 for warnings

curr.definition: ISO currency code (USD, CAD, EUR, JPY)
curr.usage: Filter by currency for single-currency analysis. Cannot aggregate different currencies without FX conversion

sec_desc.usage: Use for display and text search. Not suitable for precise filtering

issuer_nm.usage: Use for reporting and display. May duplicate letter_nm for desk-level limits

industry.definition: Industry sector (Energy, Financials, Money Markets, Environmental)
industry.usage: Filter by industry for sector-specific analysis

region_cd.definition: Geographic region: ASIA, CANADA, EMEA, AMERICAS
region_cd.usage: WHERE region_cd = 'CANADA' for regional filtering. Can infer from letter_nm if missing

state.definition: Operational state values: Approved, Pending, Rejected
state.usage: Filter by approval status: WHERE state = 'Approved' for approved limits

extension.definition: Extension field will have a value for the extended total limit when an extension is granted. When a limit extension is active, this field contains the extended limit amount.
extension.usage: Check for active extensions: WHERE extension IS NOT NULL AND extension != 0. Check end_dt for expiry date

end_dt.usage: Monitor WHERE extension IS NOT NULL AND end_dt <= MAX(date) + INTERVAL '7 days' for imminent expiry

id1.usage: Internal reference. Not typically used in user queries.

id2.usage: Use pattern matching: WHERE id2 LIKE '%-PRIMARY' for primary limits. Contains limit_id + class suffix.

grid_cc_id.usage: Internal grid reference. Not typically used in queries.

grid_cell_id.definition: Grid cell identifier for grid-based limits
grid_cell_id.usage: Used for grid-based aggregation. Example values: '0', '0.6704'

cur_id.usage: Internal currency reference. Use 'curr' column for filtering by currency.

sec_id.usage: Reference to specific security. May be null for desk-level limits.

issuer_id.usage: Links to issuer_nm. Used for issuer-level filtering.

ind_class_id.usage: Links to industry classification. May be null.

region_id.usage: Numeric region code. Use region_cd for filtering.

wf_instance_id.usage: Links to approval workflows. Used with 'state' field for workflow tracking.

st_dt.usage: Start date for limit validity or extension period. Format: YYYY-MM-DD

limit_concatenate.definition: Concatenated limit identifier string for display
limit_concatenate.usage: Human-readable concatenated identifier (e.g., '3116802 / EQ VEGA /'). Use for display only.

pref_name.usage: Short display name (e.g., 'Oil Prod Limit'). Use for reporting/display.

LM_Column1.usage: Internal metadata field. Not typically used in user queries.

LM_Column2.usage: Internal metadata field. Not typically used in user queries.

LM_Column3.usage: Internal metadata field. Not typically used in user queries.

LM_Column4.usage: Internal metadata field. Not typically used in user queries.

market_risk_limits_overview.definition: Enhanced market risk exposures system controlling exposure to market movements across all asset classes (rates, prices, FX, credit). Each limit has: (1) Risk metric (PV01, Delta, Gamma, Vega, VaR); (2) Risk measure (dollar amount), (3) Threshold (limit value). Utilization = exposure_amt / effective_limit. Breach = utilization >= 1.0.

key_metrics.PV01: Interest rate sensitivity (dollar value of 1bp rate change) — includes Base PV01, PV01 by Curve
key_metrics.Delta: Price sensitivity change in value per $1 move in underlying — EQ DELTA, Oil Products Delta
key_metrics.Gamma: Delta sensitivity (convexity risk) — IR GAMMA, EQ GAMMA, 10 BPS IR GAMMA
key_metrics.Vega: Volatility sensitivity — IR VEGA, EQ VEGA, FX VEGA, commodity vegas
key_metrics.VaR: Value at Risk — potential loss at confidence level over time horizon
key_metrics.Stress limits: Scenario-based limits simulating severe and plausible stress conditions
key_metrics.Credit Limits: single name and aggregated traded credit line limits

market_risk_limits_overview.limit_hierarchy: Trading Desk → Risk Category (limit_group) → Limit Type (limit_type) → Specific Limit → Workflow State
market_risk_limits_overview.usage: Essential context for understanding limit structure and risk metrics.

default_behaviors.description: Implicit defaults to apply when certain parameters are not specified by user. Apply defaults CONDITIONALLY - only when query is ambiguous or doesn't specify.

defaults.apply_when: ONLY if query mentions 'primary' OR query is ambiguous (e.g., 'show me limits' without desk/metric). DO NOT apply if query is specific (e.g., 'show me Canadian Options PV01 Delta limits in CAD')
defaults.conditional_logic: If query specifies desk + metric + unit, skip this default. If query is vague or mentions 'primary', apply it.

defaults.sql_pattern: ORDER BY utilization DESC LIMIT N
defaults.apply_when: When query mentions 'top', 'highest', or ranking concepts
When filtering by approval status is needed. Default to approved limits unless user specifies otherwise.

defaults.sql_pattern: Do NOT add LIMIT unless user explicitly specifies a number (e.g., 'top 5', 'top 10')
defaults.apply_when: Only if user explicitly says 'top N' with a number. For 'top' without number, return all results sorted appropriately

default_behaviors.important_note: If query is specific (desk + metric + unit specified), don't add unnecessary defaults. Only apply defaults when query is ambiguous or missing critical information.

common_query_patterns.description: Typical query patterns and how to translate them to SQL

patterns.description: Users often want to see all limits for a specific trading desk or business unit they own/manage
user_query_examples: show me limits for Canadian Options
what are the Canadian Money Markets limits
patterns.sql_template: SELECT * FROM limits_data WHERE letter_nm = '{desk_name}' AND date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY utilization DESC

patterns.pattern_name: View limits by limit_group (risk metric type)
patterns.description: Users want to see all limits of a specific risk type across all desks
patterns.sql_template: SELECT * FROM limits_data WHERE limit_group LIKE '%{risk_metric}%' AND limit_class = 'Primary' AND date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY utilization DESC LIMIT 10
patterns.critical_note: Use limit_group with pattern matching LIKE '%{metric}%' (NOT limit_type) when user mentions metric name. Many limit_groups have letter prefixes (A., B., C., etc.)

patterns.description: Users want to see the highest utilized limits. If metric specified, filter by limit_group. Default N=10, sort by utilization DESC
patterns.sql_template: SELECT * FROM limits_data WHERE {metric_filter} limit_class = 'Primary' AND date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY utilization DESC LIMIT {N}
patterns.note: If metric specified: add WHERE limit_group LIKE '%{metric}%' AND. Use limit_group with pattern matching (NOT limit_type)

patterns.description: Filter by utilization threshold to find breaches or near-breaches
patterns.sql_template: SELECT * FROM limits_data WHERE utilization >= {threshold} AND date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY utilization DESC

patterns.description: Filter limits by region code or derive from letter_nm
patterns.sql_template: SELECT * FROM limits_data WHERE region_cd = '{region}' AND date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY utilization DESC LIMIT 10

critical_field_mapping.description: CRITICAL: Many limit_groups start with letters (A., B., C., etc.). When users mention 'PV01', 'Gamma', 'Liquidity', etc., they refer to limit_group, NOT limit_type. Use pattern matching for limit_group.
critical_field_mapping.rule: User query 'PV01 limits' → WHERE limit_group LIKE '%PV01%' OR limit_group = 'C. PV01 Curve Risk Limits' (NOT limit_type LIKE '%PV01%')

examples.incorrect: WHERE limit_group = 'PV01' (no exact match - use pattern matching) OR WHERE limit_type = 'PV01' (limit_type is 'PV01 Delta', not 'PV01')

examples.user_query: show me Primary PV01 limits for Canadian Options desk for the latest 7 days
examples.correct: WHERE letter_nm = 'Canadian Options' AND limit_group LIKE '%PV01%' AND limit_class = 'Primary' AND date >= MAX(date) - INTERVAL '7 days'
examples.incorrect: WHERE limit_group = 'PV01' (will return 0 rows - use pattern matching) OR WHERE limit_type = 'PV01' (limit_type is 'PV01 Delta')

clarification_rules.description: Rules for when to ask for clarification vs. proceeding with defaults or best-effort interpretation

when_to_clarify.clarification_question: By 'high utilization', do you mean above 90%, 95%, or breached (100%)?
when_to_clarify.decision: CLARIFY if no numeric hint (e.g., '>0.9', 'above 90%'). PROCEED if numeric hint present.

when_to_clarify.scenario: Partial desk name that could match multiple
when_to_clarify.example: 'Canadian' could match 'Canadian Options', 'Canadian Money Markets', 'Canadian Prime Finance'
when_to_clarify.clarification_question: Which Canadian desk? (Canadian Options, Canadian Money Markets, Canadian Prime Finance, or all Canadian desks?)
when_to_clarify.decision: CLARIFY if partial name matches 3+ desks. PROCEED if matches 1-2 desks or user says 'all'.

when_to_clarify.example: 'sum of exposure' when data has USD, CAD, EUR
when_to_clarify.clarification_question: Which currency? (USD, CAD, EUR, or sum all currencies?)
when_to_clarify.decision: CLARIFY if aggregation requested and multiple currencies present. PROCEED if single currency or user specifies.

when_to_clarify.scenario: Limit ID missing + query would return multiple rows
when_to_clarify.clarification_question: Which desk or limit? (This would return many limits)
when_to_clarify.decision: CLARIFY if query is too broad. PROCEED if query is specific enough.

when_not_to_clarify.action: PROCEED - use conversation history to resolve pronouns

when_not_to_clarify.example: 'show me Canadian Options PV01 Delta limits in CAD'

specific_clarifying_questions: By 'high utilization', do you mean above 90%, 95%, or breached (100%)?
Which desk? (Canadian Options, Canadian Money Markets, or all Canadian desks?)
Which currency? (USD, CAD, EUR, or sum all currencies?)
Which date or date range? (latest snapshot, last 7 days, specific date?)

Combine previous WHERE with new condition

aggregation_patterns.description: Keyword mapping and rules for handling aggregation queries

currency_handling.rule: Cannot aggregate different currencies without conversion. If aggregation requested and multiple currencies present, either filter by currency or clarify with user.
currency_handling.example: 'sum of exposure' when data has USD, CAD, EUR → either filter WHERE meas_unit = 'USD' or ask user which currency

examples.sql: SELECT SUM(exposure_amt) AS total_exposure FROM limits_data WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data)
examples.note: If multiple currencies, filter by currency or clarify

complex_query_examples.description: Complex SQL queries requiring multiple filters, date ranges, aggregations, and advanced SQL features

examples.query: show me Canadian PV01 limits over the past 2 weeks
examples.sql: SELECT date, limit_id, letter_nm, limit_type, limit_group, meas_unit, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization FROM limits_data WHERE letter_nm LIKE '%Canadian%' AND limit_group = 'PV01' AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '13 days' AND date <= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY date DESC, utilization DESC

examples.query: show me limits that breached (utilization >= 1.0) in the last 10 days
examples.sql: SELECT date, limit_id, letter_nm, limit_type, limit_group, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, extension FROM limits_data WHERE utilization >= 1.0 AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '9 days' AND date <= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY date DESC, utilization DESC

examples.query: how has exposure changed for stress limits in CAD currency over the past week
examples.sql: SELECT date, limit_id, letter_nm, limit_type, meas_unit, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, (exposure_amt - LAG(exposure_amt) OVER (PARTITION BY limit_id ORDER BY date)) AS exposure_change FROM limits_data WHERE limit_group = 'Stress Limits' AND meas_unit = 'CAD' AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '6 days' AND date <= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY date DESC, limit_id
examples.key_learning: Use limit_group = 'Stress Limits' (NOT limit_type LIKE '%Stress%'). Window functions for day-over-day comparisons

examples.query: show me average utilization by limit group over the past week
examples.sql: SELECT limit_group, COUNT(DISTINCT limit_id) AS num_limits, AVG(utilization) AS avg_utilization, MAX(utilization) AS max_utilization, MIN(utilization) AS min_utilization FROM limits_data WHERE date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '6 days' AND date <= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) GROUP BY limit_group ORDER BY avg_utilization DESC
examples.key_learning: Use GROUP BY with COUNT, AVG, MAX, MIN for summary statistics

query_reference.description: Comprehensive SQL query reference guide with 16 common queries plus utility queries. Each query includes SQL and a concise explanation for senior data analysts.

common_queries.title: Show me latest data
common_queries.sql: SELECT * FROM limits_data WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) ORDER BY limit_id, date DESC;
common_queries.explanation: Retrieves all records for the most recent date in the dataset by using a subquery to find the maximum date, then filtering and ordering by limit_id and date.

common_queries.title: Show me breached limits (utilization >= 1.0)
common_queries.sql: SELECT date, letter_nm, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, curr, state FROM limits_data WHERE utilization >= 1.0 ORDER BY utilization DESC, date DESC;
common_queries.explanation: Filters records where utilization is greater than or equal to 1.0 (100%), indicating the limit has been breached, and orders by utilization severity and date.

common_queries.title: Show me limits near breach (utilization >= 0.9)
common_queries.sql: SELECT date, letter_nm, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, curr, state FROM limits_data WHERE utilization >= 0.9 AND utilization < 1.0 ORDER BY utilization DESC, date DESC;
common_queries.explanation: Identifies limits at risk of breach by filtering utilization between 0.9 (90%) and 1.0, excluding already breached limits, sorted by proximity to breach threshold.

common_queries.title: Show me PV01 limits for Canadian Options
common_queries.user_query: Show me PV01 limits for Canadian Options
common_queries.sql: SELECT date, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, curr, state FROM limits_data WHERE letter_nm = 'Canadian Options' AND limit_type = 'PV01 Delta' ORDER BY date DESC, limit_id;
common_queries.explanation: Filters by desk name 'Canadian Options' and limit type 'PV01 Delta' to retrieve all PV01-related limits for this specific desk, ordered chronologically.

common_queries.title: Show me limits with active extensions
common_queries.user_query: Show me limits with active extensions
common_queries.sql: SELECT date, letter_nm, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, extension, st_dt, end_dt, state FROM limits_data WHERE extension = 1 ORDER BY date DESC, limit_id;
common_queries.explanation: Returns all limits where the extension flag equals 1, indicating an active extension is in place, including extension start and end dates for reference.

common_queries.title: Show me Primary limits only
common_queries.sql: SELECT date, letter_nm, limit_id, id2, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, state FROM limits_data WHERE id2 LIKE '%-PRIMARY' ORDER BY date DESC, limit_id;
common_queries.explanation: Filters records where the id2 column contains '-PRIMARY' suffix, identifying primary limits (as opposed to secondary limits), using LIKE pattern matching for flexibility.

trend_analysis_queries.title: Show me Canadian Options PV01 limit for the past 7 days
trend_analysis_queries.user_query: Show me Canadian Options PV01 limit for the past 7 days
trend_analysis_queries.sql: SELECT date, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, curr FROM limits_data WHERE letter_nm = 'Canadian Options' AND limit_type = 'PV01 Delta' AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '7 days' ORDER BY date DESC, limit_id;
trend_analysis_queries.explanation: Retrieves PV01 Delta limits for Canadian Options desk over the last 7 days using date arithmetic relative to the maximum date in the dataset, providing a week-over-week trend view of limit utilization.

trend_analysis_queries.title: What is the SET Management Gamma limit for the past week
trend_analysis_queries.user_query: What is the SET Management Gamma limit for the past week
trend_analysis_queries.sql: SELECT date, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, curr FROM limits_data WHERE letter_nm = 'SET Management' AND limit_type = 'Gamma Vega' AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '7 days' ORDER BY date DESC;
trend_analysis_queries.explanation: Filters for SET Management desk's Gamma Vega limits over the past 7 days relative to the latest date in the dataset, showing daily exposure and utilization trends for gamma risk limits.

trend_analysis_queries.title: Show me limit and exposure for limit id 300128 for past 7 days
trend_analysis_queries.user_query: Show me limit and exposure for limit id 300128 for past 7 days
trend_analysis_queries.sql: SELECT date, letter_nm, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, Original_limit, effective_limit, utilization, curr, state FROM limits_data WHERE limit_id = 300128 AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '7 days' ORDER BY date DESC;
trend_analysis_queries.explanation: Provides a historical view of a specific limit (300128) showing both original and effective limits alongside actual exposure over the past week relative to the latest date, for trend analysis.

trend_analysis_queries.title: Show me Primary PV01 limits for Canadian Options desk for the latest 7 days
trend_analysis_queries.user_query: Show me Primary PV01 limits for Canadian Options desk for the latest 7 days
trend_analysis_queries.sql: SELECT date, limit_id, id2, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, curr FROM limits_data WHERE letter_nm = 'Canadian Options' AND limit_type = 'PV01 Delta' AND id2 LIKE '%-PRIMARY' AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '7 days' ORDER BY date DESC, limit_id;
trend_analysis_queries.explanation: Combines multiple filters (desk, limit type, primary status, and date range) to show only primary PV01 limits for Canadian Options over the past week relative to the latest date, excluding secondary limits.

complex_queries.title: Show me Canadian PV01 limits over the past 2 weeks
complex_queries.user_query: Show me Canadian PV01 limits over the past 2 weeks
complex_queries.sql: SELECT date, letter_nm, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, curr FROM limits_data WHERE letter_nm LIKE '%Canadian%' AND limit_type = 'PV01 Delta' AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '14 days' ORDER BY letter_nm, date DESC, limit_id;
complex_queries.explanation: Uses LIKE pattern matching to capture all Canadian desks (e.g., Canadian Options, Canadian Prime Finance) and filters PV01 Delta limits over 14 days relative to the latest date, grouped by desk for comparison.

complex_queries.title: Show me limits that breached in the last 10 days
complex_queries.user_query: Show me limits that breached in the last 10 days
complex_queries.sql: SELECT date, letter_nm, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, curr, state FROM limits_data WHERE utilization >= 1.0 AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '10 days' ORDER BY date DESC, utilization DESC;
complex_queries.explanation: Identifies all breached limits (utilization >= 1.0) within the last 10 days relative to the latest date, ordered by date and severity, to track recent limit violations for risk management review.

complex_queries.title: How has exposure changed for stress limits in CAD currency over the past week
complex_queries.user_query: How has exposure changed for stress limits in CAD currency over the past week
complex_queries.sql: SELECT date, letter_nm, limit_id, limit_desc, exposure_amt, effective_limit, utilization, LAG(exposure_amt) OVER (PARTITION BY limit_id ORDER BY date) AS previous_exposure, exposure_amt - LAG(exposure_amt) OVER (PARTITION BY limit_id ORDER BY date) AS exposure_change FROM limits_data WHERE limit_group = 'Stress Limits' AND curr = 'CAD' AND date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '7 days' ORDER BY limit_id, date;
complex_queries.explanation: Uses window functions (LAG) to calculate day-over-day exposure changes for stress limits in CAD, showing both current exposure and the delta from the previous day for trend analysis over the past week.

complex_queries.title: Show me average utilization by limit group over the past week
complex_queries.user_query: Show me average utilization by limit group over the past week
complex_queries.sql: SELECT limit_group, COUNT(DISTINCT limit_id) AS num_limits, AVG(utilization) AS avg_utilization, MAX(utilization) AS max_utilization, MIN(utilization) AS min_utilization FROM limits_data WHERE date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL '6 days' AND date <= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) GROUP BY limit_group ORDER BY avg_utilization DESC;
complex_queries.explanation: Aggregates utilization metrics by limit_group using GROUP BY, calculating average, max, and min utilization along with count of unique limits to identify which limit groups are most utilized over the past week.

complex_queries.title: How many limits are breached?
complex_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT limit_id) AS breached_limit_count, COUNT(*) AS total_breach_records FROM limits_data WHERE utilization >= 1.0 AND date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data);
complex_queries.explanation: Counts distinct breached limits and total breach records for the latest date, providing both unique limit count and total breach instances (accounting for multiple dates per limit).

complex_queries.title: Total exposure by desk
complex_queries.sql: SELECT letter_nm, COUNT(DISTINCT limit_id) AS limit_count, SUM(exposure_amt) AS total_exposure, AVG(utilization) AS avg_utilization, MAX(utilization) AS max_utilization FROM limits_data WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) GROUP BY letter_nm ORDER BY total_exposure DESC;
complex_queries.explanation: Aggregates exposure metrics by desk for the latest date, showing total exposure, limit count, and utilization statistics to identify desks with highest exposure and risk concentration.

utility_queries.title: Get all unique desks
utility_queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT letter_nm FROM limits_data ORDER BY letter_nm;
utility_queries.explanation: Returns a list of all unique desk names in the dataset for reference when building desk-specific queries.

utility_queries.title: Get all limit types
utility_queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT limit_type FROM limits_data ORDER BY limit_type;
utility_queries.explanation: Lists all distinct limit types available in the dataset (e.g., PV01 Delta, Gamma Vega, Stress Limits) for query construction reference.

utility_queries.title: Date range in dataset
utility_queries.sql: SELECT MIN(date) AS earliest_date, MAX(date) AS latest_date, COUNT(DISTINCT date) AS total_days FROM limits_data;
utility_queries.explanation: Provides the date range and total number of distinct dates in the dataset, useful for validating date filters in trend queries.

notes.date_handling: The queries use (SELECT MAX(date) FROM limits_data) - INTERVAL 'N days' syntax which is DuckDB compatible and works relative to the actual data in the table, not the current system date. This ensures queries work correctly even with historical datasets.
notes.table_name: When loading the CSV into DuckDB, the table name will be limits_data (derived from filename). If using a different name, update all queries accordingly.
notes.utilization_calculation: Utilization is already calculated in the dataset as exposure_amt / effective_limit. The queries filter on this pre-calculated value.
notes.primary_vs_secondary: The id2 column contains values like '300001-PRIMARY' or '300002-SECONDARY'. Use pattern matching with LIKE to filter.
notes.extension_flag: The extension column is binary (0 or 1), where 1 indicates an active extension.
notes.performance: For large datasets, consider adding indexes on frequently filtered columns (date, limit_id, letter_nm, limit_type) if your database supports them.
notes.column_names: All column names match exactly as they appear in the CSV header. Note that Original_limit has a capital 'O' and effective_limit is lowercase.
notes.date_range: The current dataset spans from 2024-10-09 to 2024-11-08. Queries using relative date intervals (e.g., 'past 7 days') will work correctly as long as there is sufficient historical data in the table.
